title: examples(structured): add schema-validated structured output example + retry + JSON decode helpers
author: Mateusz Zielinski
release_notes:
- Go SDK: add canonical structured output example w/ JSON schema validation and a retry strategy for parse/validation failures
- Go SDK: add small decode helpers to avoid silent JSON parse failures and improve error messages
description:
Motivation
We’ve had repeated drift and ambiguity in structured output examples (some older snippets imply “just json.Unmarshal” is sufficient). In practice, customers hit: (1) invalid JSON (trailing prose), (2) shape mismatches vs schema, (3) silent partial decoding when using permissive patterns.

This PR adds a canonical Go example for structured output that matches the cross-SDK canonical flow: request with schema, decode strictly, validate, retry on transient parse/validation failures with an explicit cap and backoff.

What’s included
- New examples/structured/ directory:
  - examples/structured/README.md: runnable instructions and expected outputs
  - examples/structured/extract_entities.go: end-to-end example (request -> validate -> retry -> final typed output)
  - examples/structured/schema.go: JSON Schema definition used by the example
- Helper utilities for decoding + error reporting:
  - internal/structured/decode.go: strict JSON decoding (disallow unknown fields, no trailing tokens)
  - internal/structured/errors.go: typed errors (ErrInvalidJSON, ErrSchemaMismatch) to drive retry decisions
- Retry strategy:
  - retry only on parse/validation errors
  - do not retry on auth/429/5xx here (that remains covered by the generic client retry guidance)
  - capped attempts (default 2 retries) + small jittered backoff

Example behavior (high level)
1) Send request with response_format={ type: "json_schema", json_schema: { name, schema, strict: true } }
2) On response:
   - strictly decode JSON (fail if there’s trailing text)
   - validate against schema (fast local validation)
3) If decode/validation fails:
   - re-ask with a short “repair” instruction that includes the validation error summary
   - retry up to N times

Implementation details
- decodeStrict uses json.Decoder with DisallowUnknownFields() and ensures there are no remaining tokens after the first value. This avoids common “it decoded but ignored trailing junk” surprises.
- schema validation uses the lightweight validator we already vendor for examples (kept in examples-only scope; no new dependency pulled into the library API surface).
- errors include the truncated response body (first 2KB) to keep logs useful while reducing accidental leakage. The README also reminds users to redact in production.

Illustrative snippet (from the example)
  type Entity struct {
    Name string `json:"name"`
    Type string `json:"type"`
  }

  var out struct {
    Entities []Entity `json:"entities"`
  }

  if err := structured.DecodeAndValidateStrict(resp.OutputText(), &out, schemaBytes); err != nil {
    // retry w/ repair prompt
  }

Notes / compatibility
- No breaking API changes in the SDK.
- Helpers live under internal/structured (example support), so we don’t commit to them as stable public API yet.

Follow-ups
- Once parity work lands in docs-site, we should link directly to this folder from the Go SDK README and the docs “Structured output” page.

Refs
- ENG-2845 (Go SDK example refresh)
- SUP-18433 (schema mismatch from older snippet)
- Canonical patterns doc: Streaming + Tools + Structured Output (Confluence)

review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan (review): The flow matches the canonical doc. Two asks: (1) make sure we’re not retrying on non-deterministic server errors here; keep it scoped to parse/validation. (2) Add a note about strict decoding (unknown fields + trailing tokens) and why it matters.
Mateusz Zielinski (author): Updated retry to only trigger on ErrInvalidJSON/ErrSchemaMismatch; other errors bubble. Added README section “Why strict decoding”.
Brian Murphy (review): Error messages look good. Can we ensure the “trailing token” case is caught? That’s the common “JSON + explanation text” failure. Also please cap logged body length.
Mateusz Zielinski (author): Added explicit decoder.More()/Token check after first decode and cap body snippet at 2KB; tests cover trailing prose case.

Marcus Lin (security review): +1 on body cap. Please add a comment that response bodies can contain sensitive user data and should be redacted before logging in production snippets. Also avoid including any tool-like execution examples here.
Mateusz Zielinski (author): Added redaction guidance + avoided logging the raw body by default (only included in error as truncated snippet). No tool execution in this example.
Elliot Price (docs review): Minor wording: use “tool calling” vs “function calling” elsewhere; here please say “structured output (JSON schema)” consistently. Also link to docs page placeholder.
Mateusz Zielinski (author): Updated terminology and linked to docs anchor (to be updated when docs PR merges).
Ibrahim Khan (approval): Approved. This unblocks the Go side of the canonical structured output examples.
